summary: National Geographic: generally believed blocks moved up large ramps greased by water/wet clay using sledges, ropes, rollers, levers; external zig-zag/spiral vs controversial internal ramp.
content: It's generally believed that the Egyptians moved massive stone blocks to the heights along large ramps, greased by water or wet clay, using a system of sledges, ropes, rollers, and levers. Some suggest exterior ramps either zig-zagged or spiraled around each pyramid, while a more controversial theory suggests internal ramps were used. Materials included granite from Aswan, copper tools, timber from Lebanon, cattle from Nile Delta farms.
